title: Jacob Boehme: His Life and Teaching, or Studies in Theosophy (account of Boehme's illumination of 1600)
author: Hans L. Martensen, reporting Abraham von Franckenberg's memoir of Jakob Boehme (1575-1624)
edition_cited: London: Hodder and Stoughton, 1885. archive.org scan jacobboehmehisli00mart
seen_via: Martensen 1885, biographical chapter, retelling Franckenberg; Boehme's own words are quoted only in part
locator_hints: Biographical chapter 'Jacob Böhme' (lines 630-680 of the saved file): seven days 'inwardly surrounded by a Divine light'; 1600, 'his eye fell upon a burnished pewter dish, which reflected the sunshine with such marvellous splendour that he fell into an inward ecstasy'; he went out on the green to banish it and found he 'gazed into the very heart of things'
summary: A nineteenth-century study of Boehme whose opening biographical chapter retells the story told by his friend Franckenberg. As a journeyman Boehme spent seven days 'inwardly surrounded by a Divine light' while working normally. In 1600, sitting in his room, his eye fell on a burnished pewter dish reflecting sunshine so brilliantly that he fell into an inward ecstasy and seemed to see into the foundations of things; thinking it fancy he walked out onto the green, where the seeing continued and matched what he saw outdoors in herbs and grass. A third experience followed in 1610. The account is third-person, gives no method, and presents the glint as an accidental trigger; what was 'seen' afterwards is insight into nature rather than light.
why_relevant: A much-cited case of a bright reflective surface triggering an altered state that persisted after the stimulus; it is second-hand and unsought, so it is marginal on the inclusion test.

date_evidence.basis: archive.org metadata year 1885; translator's preface in the saved text dated Sept. 1885

found_via: seed lead; archive.org search after rejecting Hartmann 1891 (omits the dish episode; poor OCR) and the 1764 Law edition (long-s OCR unusable)
notes: Not first-person and not a practice: likely keep_marginal or drop (spontaneous_no_practice_context). Boehme's own description of the breakthrough is in Aurora ch. 19, which says nothing of the dish; no usable public-domain English text of it was saved.
